rationale: In Spanish the "&" symbol is not used as a conjunction; it should be "y". Spanish also uses sentence case for such labels.
summary: The ampersand is kept instead of the Spanish conjunction "y", and "Privacidad"/"Seguridad" are capitalized mid-phrase.

current: ¿Estás seguro que desea eliminar esta carpeta y su contenido?
rationale: The string starts with the informal "Estás" but then switches to the formal "desea"; also "seguro que" is a queísmo, the correct form is "seguro de que". The rest of the batch uses the informal tú form consistently.
suggest: ¿Estás seguro de que quieres eliminar esta carpeta y su contenido?
summary: Mixed forms of address (tú/usted) within one sentence and missing preposition "de" in "estás seguro que".

rationale: In X.509 certificates the "Subject" is the entity the certificate is issued to; the sibling string SubjectAltNames correctly uses "sujeto", making this both wrong and inconsistent within the same screen.
summary: "Subject Name" (certificate subject) is translated as "Nombre del asunto" (name of the topic/matter) instead of the certificate term "sujeto".

current: puede cerrar sesión en los sitios web
rationale: The source says the removal may log the user out; the Spanish as written reads as if the action closes a session generically, omitting the user as the affected party.
suggest: puede cerrar tu sesión en los sitios web
summary: "might log you out of websites" is rendered as an impersonal "puede cerrar sesión en los sitios web", losing the meaning that the user will be logged out.

rationale: The developer comment says the string reports how many analytics trackers were blocked; "Contenido de rastreo" is the label for a different category (tracking content) and conflicts with the other tracker categories on the same screen.
summary: Analytics trackers label translated as "Contenido de rastreo" instead of referring to analytics trackers.

rationale: In es-ES Firefox, "Settings" is consistently translated as "Ajustes" (singular collective); "configuraciones" in plural is not the established term and reads as Latin American usage.

rationale: MainMenu.Submenus.Save.AddToShortcuts.Title/Subtitle translate "Shortcut(s)" as "Atajo"/"atajos"; the same term on the same screen must be consistent.
summary: "Shortcuts" is rendered as "accesos directos" here but as "atajos" in the paired Add to Shortcuts strings on the same submenu.

rationale: The source says "hit summarize" on a phone UI; "haz clic" implies a mouse click, inconsistent with the touch wording used elsewhere in the same feature (e.g. "Toca para resumir esta página").

rationale: "Penalties" is an English word; the es-ES term for a penalty shoot-out score is "penaltis" (or "penaltis"/"tanda de penaltis"), and the rest of the string is translated.

rationale: The en-US source and developer comment refer to Apple's Wallet; the product name must not be changed to Passbook.

rationale: The comment states both words are nouns in singular (Address, Search); the accessibility label refers to the address and search field.

rationale: The source says the connection is untrusted, not "not verified", and uses "This", not "Your".

rationale: Spanish does not use title case; "Nueva" should be lowercase, matching the sibling string "Abrir en una pestaña privada".

rationale: The comment says the shortcut resets the page view to the standard viewing size; "actual" is a false friend — Spanish "actual" means "current", not "real/original".

rationale: Menu.TrackingProtectionDescription.CryptominersNew uses "Los criptomineros"; the Spanish spelling is "cripto-".
